extracted.intended_audience: British Columbia secondary-school teachers and Grade 12 students (BC First Peoples 12)
extracted.subtask_description: A Grade 12 curriculum unit and teacher guide about Honouring the Children, Truth and Reconciliation, unmarked burials, Calls to Action, trauma-informed reporting, and related student investigations and projects. Includes suggested inquiry questions, activities, resources and assessment-oriented prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the purpose and audience of the TRC Calls to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Who are the Calls to Action for? (All Canadians, but particularly governments and churches.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be able to identify what needs to be done to work towards Reconciliation in Canada and who the Calls address. Examples given: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation created in response to Call to Action 80; Call to Action 43 calls on governments to adopt and implement UNDRIP (BC adopted UNDRIP in 2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the scope of the 94 Calls to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarity with the types of concerns covered by the 94 Calls to Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students may review the full list on the TRC website (link provided) and the version for younger students to build understanding of the variety of issues addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation (NCTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should know what records and work the NCTR does and where records from the TRC are housed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit the NCTR website to see the types of records and ongoing work (link provided) so students can connect primary-source material to investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect identification of unmarked burials to prior evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain what evidence exists that Indigenous and non-Indigenous people have always known about missing children from Indian Residential Schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can research earlier identifications and reports, and note that data in some tables include graves identified before Kamloops, adding to evidence that the issue was known prior to high-profile announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Protocols and Traditional Knowledge together with modern technology
rubrics_metrics.description: When investigating unmarked burials, use Indigenous Protocols and Traditional Knowledge along with modern scientific technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Line Master 3-3 on Protocols and Technology; consult the Canadian Archaeological Society backgrounder on remote sensing and grave detection (GPR) and consider the cultural/ethical implications of technical methods. Ask how Traditional Knowledge and Protocols are or will be used alongside technologies like ground-penetrating radar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the steps required to honour, identify, and return remains
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that fully honouring missing children includes excavation, identifying remains using oral histories, archaeology and forensics, and returning remains to home communities where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss the sequence and sensitivities of excavation and identification, and research current reports about progress toward identification and return (example CTV News article linked).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze official community communications for Oral Traditions and Protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify aspects of official statements (e.g., Tk’emlúps te Secwépemc news release) that reflect Oral Traditions, community responsibility, and adherence to Protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share the May 27, 2021 news release and have students highlight key phrases that stand out; prompt questions: What aspects reflect Oral Traditions? Why does the community feel responsibility? How were Protocols followed in releasing the news?

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify currency and accuracy of secondary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that secondary summaries (e.g., Wikipedia lists of reported grave sites) are current and accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should cross-check dates and sources, be cautious about relying solely on aggregated pages, and seek up-to-date primary or reputable secondary reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize TRC Calls to Action (71–76) in students' own words
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to restate Calls to Action 71 to 76 (Missing Children and Burial Information) in plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample paraphrases are provided (71: make all records on deaths available; 72: fund the Student Death Register; 73: maintain an online cemetery registry; 74: inform families and follow wishes; 75: identify, protect and commemorate burial sites). Students should practise summarizing and checking against Line Master 3-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow three principles when working on burial-site investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: When doing work related to burial sites, follow specified principles: action led by the First Nations community most affected; consult Survivors and Knowledge Keepers; respect protocols when investigating burial sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles should guide any community-engaged or investigative practice; discuss practical implications and how to implement them in research or projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice trauma-informed and culturally sensitive reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply trauma-informed ethical reporting practices when covering or studying traumatic events involving Indigenous peoples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Kelsie Kilawna’s emerging guide and essays as references. Features of trauma-informed reporting noted: taking time and care, self-location, transparency, and safety care plans for those who share stories. Discuss protocols for interviewing Survivors and respect for privacy and healing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate media coverage for ethics, perspective and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how news and media reported on unmarked graves and related Indigenous issues, including perspectives presented and ethical standards observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can analyze print and video reports (e.g., CityNews, CBC) in groups to judge ethical reporting, consider whose voices are centered, and discuss journalists' accountability and the importance of informed, authentic coverage (see Reporting in Indigenous Communities resource).

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen for desired outcomes in survivor/community testimonies
rubrics_metrics.description: As students view survivor or community interviews, identify what speakers are calling for (e.g., accountability, Special Prosecutor, listening to Survivors, follow TRC Calls to Action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific video examples (CityNews, Michael Redhead Champagne) and have students note significant points, such as survivor knowledge that some children didn’t survive and questions about national accountability and reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize public and institutional reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze different reactions to news of unmarked graves and consider why some segments of the public are responding now when similar evidence existed earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompts encourage discussion about emotional connection, prior indifference, and words to describe the governmental and societal response (e.g., amnesia, apathy, indifference, ignorance, racist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss and assign responsibility for addressing past injustices
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflect on who should be responsible for identifying and returning missing children and for broader actions toward justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group work should address: Who should deal with these issues? Discrepancies and inequalities in the work; what governments and churches are doing; and whether First Nations should bear the lead responsibility. Research whether independent criminal investigations or a Special Prosecutor have been proposed/taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and justify the need for independent investigation / Special Prosecutor
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate the calls for independent criminal investigations and the appointment of a Special Prosecutor; evaluate reasons for independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can research contemporary actions and debate why an independent investigation might be important for fairness, trust, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess credibility and reliability of advocacy/tracking websites (Indigenous Watchdog)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate websites tracking Calls to Action for credibility and use them to assess progress on Calls to Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the site’s About page to determine creators and motivations; on the Calls to Action tab compare counts of Complete/In Progress/Stalled/Not Started and click into items for detailed updates (links provided). Students should produce summaries of progress for Missing Children and Burials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on current verification work at specific residential schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and report on what is currently happening at particular residential school sites regarding verification and investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use news reports and preliminary workplans (example: St. Paul’s investigation) to find who is responsible, what steps are planned, and how churches/schools are involved. Produce group reports on a chosen school.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document community healing and commemoration efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: Find examples of community healing—memorials, commemorations, walks, planting trees—and report on how communities are honouring missing children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work in pairs/groups to present findings as short reports or a class gallery of posters; look for demonstrations of commitment and strength in these activities (examples and links provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the National Student Memorial Register for structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at how the National Student Memorial Register was created, how it is presented online, and what information it contains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should compare the register’s presentation to expectations set out in Call to Action 72 and consult Indigenous Watchdog’s update on Call 72 for progress commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate the creation, recognition, and meaning of National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand how September 30 became a statutory national day, its links to advocacy, and how it can be recognized meaningfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CBC and timeline resources (Line Master 3-7) to study the role of advocates (e.g., Phyllis Webstad, Georgina Jolibois). Conduct surveys about recognition, examine provincial responses, and create ways to explain the day’s purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design meaningful commemorations (vs. token gestures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be able to propose commemorations that are meaningful rather than merely symbolic acknowledgements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss features that make commemorations meaningful; have students create paragraphs, posters, role plays or plans showing why chosen activities are substantive rather than perfunctory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess ethical sourcing and cultural appropriation of Every Child Matters merchandise
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether sellers of orange shirts and 'Every Child Matters' merchandise are ethically producing and marketing these items and whether artists’ designs have been appropriated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should check retailer information such as brand name, manufacturer, and country shipped from; discuss profit motives and cultural appropriation as part of a larger conversation about respectful support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore Jordan’s Principle and evaluate implementation progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Research what Jordan’s Principle is, its history, tribunal rulings on government interpretation, and current implementation status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should use background resources (Canadian Encyclopedia, FN Caring Society) and Indigenous Watchdog updates to determine what changes have been made to fully implement Jordan’s Principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify advocates and avenues for student advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about key advocates for Indigenous children (e.g., Cindy Blackstock) and organizations (First Nations Caring Society) and identify concrete actions students can take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can explore 'What Can You Do' pages for seven suggested actions, consider nominees for the Peter Henderson Bryce Award, and learn how advocacy led to policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss and assess the use of the term 'genocide' and 'cultural genocide'
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the evidence and arguments for labeling historical treatment of Indigenous peoples as genocide or cultural genocide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have students consult TRC reports, news coverage of judicial statements, Canadian Encyclopedia pieces, and UN definitions to compare terms (assimilation vs genocide vs cultural genocide) and evaluate supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relate the Indigenous protocol of witnessing to TRC hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand witnessing as a cultural practice and how Protocols of Witnessing were followed in TRC hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read Line Master 3-6 on Protocols of Witnessing, discuss examples of witnessing in cultural practices (feasts, potlatches), and reflect on the strength required by Elders and Survivors to provide testimony (questions provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sensitive to triggering content and plan supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that material about missing children and unmarked graves may be triggering and plan classroom safety and supports accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers are advised to be aware of potential triggers for Survivors and families, provide content warnings, facilitate supportive discussions, and have plans for students who may be distressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize big ideas and identify First Peoples-led undertakings
rubrics_metrics.description: From TRC excerpts, highlight the big ideas and identify specific undertakings that resulted from First Peoples’ actions (e.g., Survivor court cases, Settlement Agreement, creating the TRC, national apology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask students to highlight one or two sentences that express big ideas and list undertakings mentioned in the text; connect to broader Unit materials (Foundations, Glossary).
